Current execution status

Source: PORTING_PLAN.md

The cleanup and R implementation are complete, with a qualified 0.1.1 performance/parity follow-up. See IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS, qualification, performance, parity and the differences register. Current evidence: 583 assertions, 92.8989% R/C++ coverage, check 0 errors / 0 warnings, 18 synthetic reference cases and a retained forest drawing. Default MAT tie differences are explicitly retained. The assessment below is the historical design baseline; its no-implementation statements are superseded.

MLV Toolbox to R: assessment and porting plan

Assessment date: 2026-10-25; revised after local Octave and Python probes. Proposed package name: mlvtoolbox.

Recommendation

Proceed with an analysis-first R package: vector drawings and contour statistics, followed by a qualified medial-axis pipeline, then stimulus manipulation and input adapters. Keep photograph-to-contour extraction optional. This order gives a useful package early while testing the hardest scientific dependency before spending time on peripheral plotting and import features.

The intended outcome is a more robust, faster implementation that, by default, uses an alternative definition wherever a demonstrated difference from the stated method exists. Preserve the scientific quantities and make all method changes explicit. Upstream outputs help explain existing behavior; independent analytical and numerical evidence decides the R behavior when an upstream implementation departs from that evidence.

This is a feasible medium-sized scientific software project. Source translation is the smaller part of the work. Correctness, robustness, computational cost, and reproducibility are acceptance criteria for each delivered capability. Record compatibility differences instead of reproducing documented edge-case behavior to obtain matching output. Claims of equivalence or speedup require executed evidence for the stated inputs, source revisions, runtimes and backends.

This document is a plan, not an implementation or a numerical qualification report. The local workspace was empty at assessment time.

Evidence and scope

Upstream: bwlabToronto/MLV_toolbox. Pinned source: f12418a5e03c2f38e222fed1dffccf42b227cd29, the main head returned by GitHub during this assessment, committed 2025-04-30.

The complete Git tree was inspected, and all 62 top-level MLVcode/*.m files were fetched. Detailed review focused on the main analysis pipelines, statistics, drawing representation, junctions, rasterization, tracing, SVG handling, and manipulation. Counts below exclude vendored code unless stated:

Component Observed size Porting implication

Nonblank lines not beginning with a MATLAB comment 2,510 A source-size indicator, not a complexity estimate

The published 2023 methods paper provides scientific definitions and example workflows. Use it alongside the pinned code: the paper predates the current SAM extraction path.

The user supplied local reference checkouts. MATLAB source was observed at MLV_toolbox/, and the Python port at vendor/pyMLV/; refresh their locations as the user finishes the vendoring layout. The MATLAB HEAD matches the pinned SHA above. Python pyMLV was pinned to 14b3183b91146b1021eb7ef97db75ad703b06832. Both tracked-file status checks were clean after the probes. Treat the reference checkouts as read-only and put diagnostic adapters outside them.

Small R arithmetic checks, upstream contour calls under Octave, one adapted Octave MAT smoke, and a Python subpixel-orientation regression were executed. See ASSESSMENT_EVIDENCE.md for inputs, outputs, source revisions, adaptations and qualification boundaries. No R implementation, end-to-end cross-language parity, speedup or image-quality result is claimed.

Octave and Python reference strategy

Use local Octave actively for the runnable MATLAB source paths. Octave 11.1.0 and image 2.20.0 are installed. Loading the image package supplies bwdist with nearest-feature indices, bwmorph, bwareaopen, and imbinarize. The current environment lacks smoothdata, knnsearch, insertShape, xmlread, and imsegsam. Record a per-operation capability matrix instead of treating either complete MATLAB compatibility or complete unavailability as the baseline.

The unmodified MAT path hits Octave’s parser at two jj++m_Neighbors8 expressions in computeGradientVectorField.m. A temporary copy changed only these expressions to explicit addition. With that adaptation, octave-cli ran a 25-by-35 synthetic MAT case, producing finite distance/AOF matrices and 44 skeleton pixels. This is an executability probe, not a correctness or performance result. Retain a SHA-bound adapter manifest for future reference runs; never silently patch the reference checkout.

Octave’s installed bwmorph explicitly documents differences from MATLAB’s skel. Distinguish analytical correctness, Octave agreement, Python agreement, and actual MATLAB agreement. MATLAB-specific evidence remains useful where proprietary rasterization or morphology affects a claim, but MATLAB access does not block building and scientifically validating the R implementation.

The Python tree has 60 top-level code modules, with 52 same-named MATLAB core counterparts and eight additional helpers. No package build metadata, automated test directory or GitHub workflow was identified in the pinned tree. Several MATLAB capabilities have no same-named Python module, including SVG import, raster rendering and RGB/edge-map extraction. Its README also reports that the medial-axis demo currently needs MATLAB-rendered input.

Review useful NumPy/SciPy/OpenCV choices and compare selected runnable functions. The Python source is a second implementation to examine, with shared lineage; agreement between the ports is not independent scientific validation.

Demonstrated and source-level Python concerns include:

  • An executed subpixel segment test returns orientation 0 degrees rather than the analytical 315 degrees because endpoints are converted to int32.
  • Branch scoring/tracing imports missing local modules: smoothData, diff, fitLineSegments, and GetConSeg.
  • The gradient-field code loads a fixed outerBoundaryOriginal.mat and opens plots; numerical computation must not depend on external diagnostic state.
  • Skeleton thresholding aliases and overwrites the flux array, and component cleanup replaces its calculated threshold with 100.
  • Branch scoring contains derivative/window differences and an uninitialized taper intermediate. These source findings require targeted execution before relying on the corresponding outputs.

The Python root declares MIT, while numerical files retain GPL notices. Include both repositories in the per-file rights inventory; the root Python license does not settle the terms for all included components.

The main MAT code is MATLAB source, not an opaque native binary. The compiled MEX dependency stack is concentrated in the legacy structured-edge backend. That makes a native R/C++ analysis implementation practical without porting the whole photograph extraction stack.

Scientific definitions and explicit changes

The definitions below establish the reference method. They do not require preserving behavior demonstrated to depart from the stated definition. Use the stated definition by default, document the changed results, and test the invariant. A substantive new estimator, skeleton method or approximation must have an explicit method identity and its own validation.

  1. Drawing geometry. A contour is an ordered numeric matrix with columns x1, y1, x2, y2, not merely an unordered collection of edges. Preserve contour identity, segment order, and pen lifts. Dimensions upstream are [width, height], whereas matrices index [row, column].

  2. Coordinates and orientation. Image y increases downward. The upstream orientation is atan2(y1-y2, x2-x1) in degrees modulo 360. Orientation histograms use modulo 180, while curvature and junction calculations retain directed orientation. Skeleton fields called X and Y actually feed MATLAB row and column indexing; adapters must make this distinction explicit.

  3. Curvature. Preserve the piecewise definition: the wrapped absolute angle change divided by the current segment length, with the last segment compared to the previous one. A single-segment contour has curvature zero. This is not interchangeable with fitting a smooth curve and taking its differential curvature.

  4. Statistics. Orientation and curvature bins collect segment length; length bins collect whole-contour length. Junction type and angle histograms count events, with per-contour participation tracked separately. Several normalized statistics are scaled per 10,000 pixels of contour length. Specify bin-edge and overflow behavior explicitly, characterize upstream differences, and test boundaries explicitly instead of inheriting the default settings of R’s hist().

  5. MAT construction. Preserve image polarity, the two distance transforms, nearest-boundary map, 60 angular samples, epsilon 1, flux thresholding, thinning, and component removal. A generic morphological skeleton is not automatically equivalent to this AOF-based transform.

  6. MAT scores. Preserve branch sampling, radius smoothing, derivative padding, window K=5, final moving mean of width 3, and the tenth-power score transformation. Taper is available but absent from the default set of three properties. Its unparameterized smoothdata() calls need explicit reference characterization.

  7. Projection and missingness. Preserve the maximum across contributing skeletal branches, tangent-point mapping and radius cutoff. Upstream converts zero-valued projected samples to missing values; determine where this means “unmapped” versus a valid zero score. The R representation should distinguish these cases.

Source anchors: contour measures, orientation, curvature, MAT extraction, branch scores, projection.

Issues to resolve before claiming compatibility

Horizontal/vertical histogram loss, the empty junction-angle dimensions, and split-budget overshoot were reproduced by running the upstream MATLAB functions in Octave. Other entries below remain source-level findings or arithmetic checks. The Python subpixel-orientation difference was executed separately.

Finding Evidence Proposed treatment
Exactly horizontal segments disappear from the horizontal/vertical histogram The Octave call on a length-10 horizontal segment returned total 0; the strict comparison excludes thisHV=1 Include the upper endpoint and require histogram mass conservation
Empty junction-angle output has inconsistent default dimensions The Octave call returned 5 histogram entries and 8 centers Return a consistent zero vector of the requested length
Omitted MAT threshold differs from explicit 28 degrees computeMAT uses 0.3 when omitted, versus 2/pi*sin(28*pi/180)=0.2988749 Make omitted and explicit threshold_angle=28 use the same conversion; retain raw-threshold control for replication
A split’s top group can exceed its requested length fraction The Octave length-ranked split of lengths 4,4,2 at fraction 0.5 retained length 8/10 at the top after sorting Enforce the documented whole-contour length budget, with deterministic ties and explicit unassigned contours
Curvature ranking description and calculation differ splitLDbyProperties describes an average but computes a length-weighted sum without dividing by contour length Preserve the actual criterion under an explicit name; add a separately named mean if useful
Zero scores and missing projections are conflated MATpropertiesToContours marks thisProp~=0 as valid Carry a separate mapping mask and test the effects of retaining valid zeros
RGB function help and actual default differ Help mentions structured-edge detection; the arguments block sets SAM Make the backend explicit and store its identity and settings

The R definition is the default. For each demonstrated difference, retain the minimal reproducing input, upstream behavior, independent expected result and regression test. Maintain a concise table of intentional differences.

Do not add a package-wide “legacy mode” prematurely. Add a narrow replication option only when a real analysis requires the historical behavior. Ambiguous scientific choices require a stated definition and evidence, rather than silently changing the quantity being measured.

Direct source: horizontal/vertical bins, empty junction output, threshold default, splitting, score missingness, RGB extraction.

Proposed R design

Use a small S3 API. Do not export 62 one-for-one wrappers.

  • mlv_drawing: ordered list of numeric segment matrices, width, height, stable contour IDs, original-image metadata, and provenance.
  • Derived segment and contour properties: explicit tables attached to the drawing or returned as tables; geometry-changing operations invalidate or recompute them. Do not retain stale cached properties after rotation or segmentation.
  • mlv_mat: signed-distance matrix, nearest-boundary indices, AOF matrix, logical skeleton, branch records, parameters, and provenance.
  • Raster data: ordinary [height, width] matrices, with TRUE meaning ink in a logical drawing mask. Convert polarity at upstream-compatible boundaries. Raster-aligned pixel centers are (1,1) at the top left. SVG coordinate transforms and clipping rules must be explicit.
  • Statistics: data frames carrying property, bin center/edges, value, units, normalization, and contour ID where relevant.

Proposed public verbs, not yet implemented:

drawing <- mlv_drawing(contours, width = 640, height = 480)
drawing <- compute_contour_properties(drawing)
stats <- contour_statistics(drawing)
plot(drawing, property = "curvature")

mask <- rasterize(drawing)
mat <- compute_mat(mask, threshold_angle = 28)
mat <- compute_mat_properties(mat, properties = c("mirror", "parallelism", "separation"))
drawing <- map_mat_properties(drawing, mat)

parts <- split_contours(drawing, property = "length", fraction = 0.5)

Provide read_mlv_mat(), read_mlv_svg(), tabular export and as.data.frame(). For model-based selection, accept an R prediction function or supported predict() method with a specified feature schema. Importing serialized MATLAB regression/ensemble objects is outside the initial scope.

Use base R for geometry, statistics, object handling and initial plots. Use Rcpp for measured hotspots and kernels requiring precise raster semantics, especially AOF and potentially distance transforms/thinning. Keep small, transparent R reference implementations for numerical kernels where feasible.

Make xml2, png, jpeg, and MATLAB-file readers optional adapters. Detect MAT-file formats before deciding how to read them. Evaluate an existing image library against fixtures before accepting its distance or morphology routines as a backend; availability of a similarly named operation is insufficient.

Avoid imposing Python, deep-learning weights, a GPU, or a large spatial stack on users who only need contour statistics. Optional RGB extraction should accept precomputed masks/labels, or use a separately configured local backend. A Canny alternative would be a different extraction method, with its own name and provenance.

Suggested package layout: R/ for objects and workflows, src/ for qualified kernels, tests/testthat/ for behavior and oracle comparisons, inst/fixtures/ for tiny reusable inputs, tools/reference/ for Octave/MATLAB reference runners and adapters, and vignettes/ for reproducible workflows.

Robustness acceptance criteria

  • Validate dimensions, finite coordinates, column meanings and segment order at construction/import boundaries. Normalize MATLAB-file nesting once at import. Preserve subpixel doubles and use explicit index conversions at native/image boundaries.
  • Define empty results with stable types and shapes. Reject or explicitly clean zero-length segments while retaining ID mappings. Undefined quantities must have documented missing/error behavior rather than arbitrary epsilon denominators that turn them into plausible scores.
  • Exercise nearly parallel/collinear segments, duplicate points, tiny branches, zero radii, extreme coordinate magnitudes, all-ink/all-background masks and border-touching shapes. Use scale-aware numerical predicates where needed; preserve separate absolute and relative gap criteria.
  • Keep zero-valued scores separate from missing mappings. Protect input arrays and AOF results from aliasing and in-place threshold side effects.
  • Derived properties must be invalidated on geometry changes. Keep IDs and tie rules stable, and expose the selected method, parameters and backend in results so analyses can be reproduced.
  • Numerical functions must run without plot windows, working-directory-specific files, implicit model downloads, unsolicited output files or network calls. Visualization and export are explicit operations.
  • Keep memory use bounded and check dimensions/index capacity before allocating. Support interruption of long native kernels and produce actionable errors.

Delivery sequence and acceptance gates

Phase 0 — Baseline, rights inventory, and reference capture

  • Freeze the source SHA, source manifest, function dependency map, and licenses.
  • Inventory rights per reused core/helper file and per candidate dataset. The README explicitly defers licensing to individual modules; several core files have GPL-3.0-or-later notices, while many others only have copyright notices. Do not assume one blanket upstream license. Resolve the package license after the inventory and any necessary maintainer clarification.
  • Establish Octave as the local reference runner, load image explicitly, and record runtime/package versions, platform, source SHA, parameters and seeds. Enumerate supported functions, unavailable operations and diagnostic adapters. Prefer octave-cli for headless runs.
  • Compare selected runnable Python paths at their pinned SHA. Record independent analytical expectations alongside the two upstream outputs; behavior the two share must not become the expected R result when it departs from the analytical expectation.
  • Capture MATLAB-specific reference evidence when available and useful for proprietary raster/morphology behavior. Its absence is a qualification boundary, not a blocker for the R package.
  • Generate synthetic fixtures in the drawing representation and as binary matrices. Export intermediate arrays, event records, bin boundaries, and branch data, not only screenshots or final image summaries.
  • Preserve NaN/Inf and dimensions in the fixture format; write a metadata manifest and convert to compact R fixtures reproducibly.
  • Use demos/testPatterns.svg as a candidate workflow fixture after rights review. Treat demos/Forest_DBW.mat as a historical example, not a newly executed oracle: its generating version is not established.

Gate: reproducible analytical fixtures, an Octave/Python capability matrix and executable reference probes, attribution/rights inventory for the first reused scope, and a table of intentional differences. Reference adapters must be visible and version-bound. Do not label an Octave run as MATLAB evidence.

Phase 1 — Useful contour-analysis package

  • Create package metadata, S3 constructors/validators, and stable IDs.
  • Implement orientation, length, curvature, junction detection/cleanup/types, histograms, summaries, and simple vector plotting.
  • Define empty-drawing, zero-length, nonfinite coordinate and disconnected segment behavior. Reject invalid inputs or provide explicit cleaning; never permit unnoticed division by zero.
  • Retain a simple exhaustive pairwise junction implementation as the small-case correctness witness. Profile representative sparse and dense drawings, then use exact spatial candidate filtering for larger inputs when it improves cost. Candidate rejection must account for the existing gap tolerances.

Gate: independent analytical fixtures and qualified upstream comparisons for supported cases, regression tests for each documented difference, and a runnable “drawing to feature table” example. This is the first useful release scope even if the MAT pipeline is still under development.

Phase 2 — Raster and MAT feasibility gate

  • Implement deterministic rasterization separately from display plotting.
  • Implement or qualify exact Euclidean distance plus nearest-feature indices, including tie rules; preserve the signed-distance construction.
  • Port AOF with the specified sampling and boundaries.
  • Reproduce or explicitly qualify thinning, component cleanup, edge linking, and branch construction. The primary tracing route is GetConSeg -> edgelink(image,10) -> cleanup, with its minimum-length and topology effects.
  • Profile the pilot on modest and larger synthetic images before expanding native-code scope.

Gate: compare each intermediate array on rectangles, disks, rings, parallel lines, border-touching shapes and junctions. Test raster masks, topology and geometric accuracy, not merely visual plausibility. Label the morphology backend. When a deliberate algorithm change alters topology, establish its scientific behavior with independent evidence and document the method difference; do not hide it by loosening comparison tolerances.

Phase 3 — Full medial-axis analysis

  • Implement parallelism, separation, mirror and taper scores with explicit smoothing/window semantics.
  • Implement tangent projection, nearest-neighbor selection, mapping masks, per-contour scores and MAT histograms.
  • Port the full drawing -> raster -> MAT -> branch scores -> contour scores -> feature-table workflow.

Gate: separate fixtures for branch formulas and geometric reconstruction, then end-to-end comparisons. Compare branch structure, score locations, missingness and histograms in addition to aggregate means.

Phase 4 — Complete the practical workflows

  • Add SVG and MATLAB drawing import, raster edge-map tracing, rotation, circular apertures, shifting, segmentation and property-based splitting.
  • Preserve the existing SVG feature set deliberately: lines, polylines, polygons, rectangles, circles/ellipses, Bezier paths, arcs and transforms. Stage this support; unsupported constructs must be reported rather than silently dropped. General SVG rendering is outside scope.
  • Implement model feature-table construction and R prediction adapters.
  • Add property plots, image exports, feature-density maps and batch examples. Consolidate MATLAB draw/render variants into a small R surface.
  • Make stochastic operations reproducible with R seeds and recorded settings; cross-language random sequences are not an initial equivalence requirement.

Gate: contour IDs/order remain traceable; transformations invalidate derived properties correctly; split lengths, ties and model schemas are tested; imports have a documented support matrix.

Phase 5 — Optional RGB backend and distribution qualification

These are separate work streams; RGB support does not gate an analysis release.

  • RGB: establish a backend contract for segmentation/edge maps, then qualify model identity, weights, preprocessing, thresholds, output masks and the shared tracing/postprocessing path. Review pyMLV as it develops; its inspected tree does not yet supply a complete extraction backend. A Python SAM bridge remains a candidate requiring its own qualification against the stated method.
  • Distribution: run package checks on macOS, Windows and Linux, native checks if C++ is included, meaningful coverage, and build the vignettes from scratch.
  • Publish documentation for contour analysis, medial-axis analysis, stimulus manipulation and optional extraction, with a feature/status matrix.

Gate: executed platform checks and reproducible examples for the advertised scope. Publication, registry submission and deployment remain separate actions.

Verification design

Use both upstream comparisons and independent evidence; reproducing upstream behavior on a documented edge case is not scientific validation.

  • Geometry fixtures: horizontal/vertical/diagonal and subpixel segments, directed reversal, one-segment contours, corners, closed loops, zero-length segments, empty drawings and large/small coordinate magnitudes.
  • Junction fixtures: T, Y, X, Arrow, Star, near misses around both epsilon thresholds, collinear/overlapping segments, nearby junction merges and same-contour self-crossings (excluded by the upstream method).
  • Raster/MAT fixtures: exact small masks, unequal image dimensions, tiny images, blank/full masks, borders, symmetric nearest-boundary ties, short branches, loops and adjacent branch points.
  • Score fixtures: constant-radius straight branches, changing radius, bent branches, endpoints and smoothing windows shorter than the data; test the final exponent explicitly.
  • Statistics: exact bin boundaries, mass conservation for applicable histograms, zero totals, nondefault bin counts and normalization units.
  • Metamorphic checks: translation preserves vector geometry statistics; rigid rotation preserves lengths and curvature; contour reversal preserves axial orientation histograms. Scaling preserves orientation and scales length/curvature inversely as appropriate. Do not assert these invariances indiscriminately for pixel-threshold junctions or raster-based scores.
  • Compare topology and identifiers exactly after a documented canonicalization of branch direction/order. Use explicit per-output floating-point tolerances selected from reference precision and sensitivity tests, not one broad tolerance that can hide skeleton changes.
  • Measure core geometry, junction search, rasterization, distance/AOF, branch tracing and mapping separately. Report input dimensions, contour counts, runtime versions, cold versus warm behavior and memory use. Do not promise a speedup before measurement.

Performance work and acceptance criteria

A faster implementation is an explicit deliverable. Start with correct small reference kernels and measured upstream baselines. Improve algorithms and data movement before introducing parallelism.

Hot path Candidate improvement Correctness witness
Junction detection Expanded bounding boxes plus a grid/sweep/spatial index, then the exact intersection predicate Exhaustive pairs on small random and adversarial drawings; sparse and dense cases
Distance transforms Linear-time exact EDT with nearest-feature coordinates; bounded working arrays Brute-force nearest-boundary search on small masks, including ties
AOF Compiled loops, precomputed samples/normal data, efficient index decoding and reusable buffers Slow scalar evaluation on tiny signed-distance/nearest-boundary inputs
Branch scores Prefix sums for fixed/local windows and shared derivative computations Direct window sums and analytical branches, including endpoints
Contour projection Exact nearest-neighbor indexing with deterministic ties; reuse geometry across properties Brute-force nearest-neighbor/tangent mapping on small drawings
Raster and feature tables Avoid drawing each full image repeatedly; reuse masks and preallocate tables Pixel fixtures, ID tracing and histogram conservation

These are candidates to measure, not established speedups. Preserve exactness where the contract requires it. Approximate search, lower image resolution, fewer AOF samples and lower numerical precision require an explicitly named method/quality tradeoff; they cannot be hidden inside a speed claim.

Plan benchmark families around 100, 1,000 and 10,000 segments (including sparse and dense junction layouts), and 128, 512 and 1,024 pixel square masks plus rectangular cases. Bound the expensive reference runs and record any cases that cannot finish within the benchmark budget.

Compare identical completed work and supported parameters against the pinned MATLAB source under Octave, runnable Python paths where available, and the simple R reference implementation. Record host, versions, threads, setup, cold/first/warm timings, allocations/peak memory, and per-stage as well as end-to-end time. Missing or failing upstream functions are capability gaps, not speedups. Separate extraction/model loading from contour analysis.

Gate: on declared representative workloads, demonstrate an end-to-end improvement and explain per-stage regressions or tradeoffs, while passing the correctness suite and memory bounds. Report measured ratios and uncertainty; set numerical performance targets after baseline profiling. Do not claim the package is faster merely because it uses compiled code.

Once a package exists, the minimum local checks will be the relevant testthat subset followed by R CMD build and R CMD check --as-cran on the produced tarball. Exact package commands and platform jobs will be recorded against the implemented revision. These checks have not been run because no R package has been implemented.

Data and dependency boundaries

Keep the user-supplied reference checkouts available locally and unchanged. Exclude full vendor checkouts, the approximately 651 MiB dataset directory and trained-model trees from the R package tarball and normal CI. Configure package build exclusions once the layout settles; this does not authorize deleting or moving the user’s reference data.

Use synthetic fixtures by default; add small real-image examples only after checking redistribution rights. Availability in an upstream repository does not establish permission for a new package distribution.

Local assessment environment: R 4.5.1; Rcpp 1.1.2, cpp11 0.5.5, testthat 3.3.2, xml2 1.6.0, png 0.1-9, jpeg 0.1-11, R.matlab 3.7.0, imager 1.0.8 and hdf5r 1.3.12 were reported installed. Package presence does not establish backend suitability. R startup emitted locale warnings. Octave 11.1.0 with image 2.20.0 is available and was exercised as described above. Python 3.14.7 with NumPy 2.4.3 ran the orientation probe; cv2 and skimage were absent from that interpreter. No MATLAB executable was found on PATH or in the standard app location. Full MATLAB equivalence remains untested.

Initial sizing: contour analysis is the smallest work package; rasterization, skeleton topology and MAT projection are the largest uncertainty. Set a calendar estimate after the Phase 0 reference capture and a Phase 2 pilot rather than estimating solely from source line counts. RGB backend work has its own model and runtime dependencies and should be estimated separately.

First implementation task

Start with manifests for both reference checkouts, the Octave runner/adaptation specification, the regression cases for known differences and the mlv_drawing contract. Implement constructors and orientation/length/curvature with subpixel and degenerate-input tests, then define histogram boundaries and junction output shapes as those APIs are added. Establish the correctness and timing harness before optimizing the expensive kernels.

This assessment updated planning/evidence documents and ran bounded synthetic probes. The user supplied the upstream checkouts; no R package, model download or publication was created.
